paragraphs.source_en: Children are, after all, remarkable creatures. Never dreaming that their father was at such a loss over what to do with them, they went on eating breakfast, each in high spirits. The troublesome one, however, was the little one. She was three years old this year, and the master's wife, showing some tact, had specially provided her with a small pair of chopsticks and a little rice bowl fit for a three-year-old child. But the little one would have none of it. She insisted on seizing her elder sisters' chopsticks and bowls, and on using tableware that was awkward for her to handle. Look out over society, and you will see that those petty men without ability or talent are the very ones who push themselves forward and long to climb into offices unsuited to them; that disposition begins to sprout entirely from this little-one stage. Since its origin is thus so ancient and so deep-rooted, it is certainly not something education or cultivation can correct; one had best give up such vain hopes at once.

paragraphs.source_en: The little one had captured from the sister beside her an enormous rice bowl and a pair of long chopsticks, made them her exclusive property, and was continually flaunting her tyranny. Because she insisted on using things she could not manage, she was forced to behave tyrannically. First she gripped the bases of the two chopsticks together in her hand and thrust them mightily down to the bottom of the bowl. The bowl was eight-tenths full of rice, and miso soup had been poured all over the top. The instant the force of the chopsticks reached the bowl, the vessel, which had somehow just managed to keep its balance, received this sudden assault and at once tilted about thirty degrees. At the same time the miso soup, without the least mercy, streamed out and spattered all over her chest. Naturally, the little one was not going to retreat over such a trifling matter. She was a tyrant, after all. This time she jerked the chopsticks she had driven into the bowl upward with all her strength, while bringing her little mouth to the rim and accepting into it as many of the flung-up grains of rice as she could. The grains that missed, together with the yellow broth, rallied to one another and flew onto the tip of her nose, her cheeks, and her chin. As for the grains that failed to land in those places and fell onto the tatami, they naturally lay outside her calculations; this was indeed a most high-handed way of eating rice. I respectfully offer this advice to the famous Mr. Kaneda and to all the men of power under heaven: if your treatment of others is like the little one's handling of her bowl and chopsticks, the grains of rice that fly into your mouths will be exceedingly few; they will not enter by any necessary momentum, but only after wandering about in confusion. I earnestly hope you will reconsider; such conduct is quite unbecoming to worldly-wise men of dexterous ability like yourselves.

paragraphs.source_en: The elder sister Tonko had had her own bowl and chopsticks plundered by the little one, and had been patiently making do with her younger sister's inappropriately tiny set; but since it was too small to begin with, even when she thought she had filled the bowl, one good opening of the mouth finished it in about three bites. Consequently her hand kept going again and again toward the rice tub. Having already refilled her bowl four times, she was now on the fifth; Tonko opened the lid of the tub, picked up the large rice paddle, and gazed at it for a while, apparently wavering over whether to eat another bowl or not. Then, seeming finally to have made up her mind, she judged a place where there was no scorched rice and scooped up a paddleful; that much went smoothly enough, but when she turned the paddle over and scraped the rice into the bowl, the rice that would not fit rolled out in lumps onto the tatami. Tonko showed not the least sign of surprise, and began carefully picking up the spilled rice. I wondered what she meant to do after picking it up. It turned out that she put it all back into the rice tub. That seems a little dirty.
